Every parameter is a control change the document says the instrument recognises, or a row of its NRPN table, with its printed name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

32 NRPN value(s) wider than 7 bits go as the document prints the format: the low bits first on their own controller, then the rest on CC 6. CEditor sends these; it does not yet put the two halves together when the instrument sends them.
Footnote *5-5 prints "TAPE BPM DOUBLING"; read as "TAPE BPM, DOUBLING": thirteen ranges are printed for what the missing comma makes twelve names
Not a parameter here, Data Entry, part of the NRPN messages: CC 6, 38.

Not a parameter here, the fine half of a pair whose coarse half is the parameter; the document does not say how many of its bits count: CC 39, 48, 49, 50, 51, 56, 58, 60, 61, 62, 63, 102, 103, 107, 108, 109, 110, 113, 114, 115, 116.
Not a parameter here, an NRPN or RPN selector, part of the NRPN messages: CC 98, 99.
Not a parameter here, a channel mode message: CC 123.

Each of these is the coarse (MSB) controller of a pair, named without "(MSB)"; it sends 0 - 127 on its own: MASTER VOLUME (CC 7, fine CC 39); EG ATTACK (CC 16, fine CC 48); EG RELEASE (CC 19, fine CC 49); TREMOLO DEPTH (CC 20, fine CC 50); TREMOLO RATE (CC 21, fine CC 51); OSC LFO RATE (CC 24, fine CC 56); OSC LFO DEPTH (CC 26, fine CC 58); MOD A (CC 28, fine CC 60); MOD B (CC 29, fine CC 61); DELAY A (CC 30, fine CC 62); DELAY B (CC 31, fine CC 63); DELAY MIX (CC 33, fine CC 113); REVERB A (CC 34, fine CC 114); REVERB B (CC 35, fine CC 115); REVERB MIX (CC 36, fine CC 116); FILTER CUTOFF (CC 43, fine CC 107); FILTER RESONANCE (CC 44, fine CC 108); FILTER SWEEP DEPTH (CC 45, fine CC 109); FILTER SWEEP RATE (CC 46, fine CC 110); OSC A (CC 54, fine CC 102); OSC B (CC 55, fine CC 103).

The document prints the program as 576Bytes (7bit) -> 505Bytes (8bit); 576 packed bytes hold 504, the size read here. Korg's own sample programs for the instrument agree: each is 504 bytes, 'PRED' at 500 - 503 where the table prints 501 - 504.

Pull: CURRENT PROGRAM DATA DUMP REQUEST, answered by the current program in Korg's 8-in-7 packing (576Bytes (7bit) -> 505Bytes (8bit)). 20 parameter(s) are read back from it by the program table's offsets; a controller parameter reads the top seven bits of its 10-bit field, the value its controller sends.

Two-byte values are read low byte first, the earlier byte holding the low eight bits: the prologue document's own TEMPO settles it (300~6000 as H:0~7 then L:0~4), and the miniKORG 700Sm's document, which prints L first, agrees.
The exclusive header carries the global MIDI channel as 3g; the profile's deviceId variable is that byte, 30H for channel 1.
In the program dump but not read back: EG TYPE (the dump names a value "ASR" the parameter has no choice for); FILTER TYPE (the dump names a value "Thru" the parameter has no choice for).

Not found under its own name in the program dump, so not read back: MASTER VOLUME, OSC TYPE, MOD TYPE, DELAY TYPE, REVERB TYPE, ARP PATTERN, ARP INTERVALS, ARP LENGTH, OSC EDIT PARAM1, OSC EDIT PARAM2, OSC EDIT PARAM3, OSC EDIT PARAM4, OSC EDIT PARAM5, OSC EDIT PARAM6, OSC EDIT PARAM7, OSC EDIT PARAM8, MOD FX EDIT PARAM1, MOD FX EDIT PARAM2, MOD FX EDIT PARAM3, MOD FX EDIT PARAM4, MOD FX EDIT PARAM5, MOD FX EDIT PARAM6, MOD FX EDIT PARAM7, MOD FX EDIT PARAM8, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM1, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM2, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM3, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM4, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM5, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM6, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM7, DELAY FX EDIT PARAM8, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM1, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM2, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM3, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM4, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM5, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM6, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM7, REVERB FX EDIT PARAM8.
